summary:
[  edit  ]
The  Pulse   CHOP  generates pulses in one channel at regular intervals. The amplitude of each pulse can be edited with the  CHOP  sliders or with handles on the graph.
The  Pulse   CHOP  gives a set of pulses in a static channel of a specifiable length.
See also the  LFO CHOP  to get an endless stream of pulses that is  Time Sliced , and the  Pattern CHOP  for a string of static pulses.
The  Pulse   CHOP  can be used as triggers to the  Copy CHOP , and can represent regularly-timed events.
By default, the pulses are a single sample long, but you can increase the  Pulse  Width so that the pulses are steps to the next pulse. You can also interpolate the values between pulses, as Linear, Ease In Ease Out, Cubic or other curves.
The pulses can be restricted to a minimum / maximum limit. If the Limit Type is Clamp, the graph has additional convenient handles at the minimum and maximum for each pulse.
The  Pulse   CHOP  generates a single channel, and you can merge several  Pulse  CHOPs into a multi-channel  CHOP .
The  Pulse   CHOP  uses its optional first input as a start/end reference, so a number of  Pulse  CHOPs can be stretched to the same interval.
The optional second input is used to specify pulses at specific sample locations. Every single-sampel input channel is then interpreted as the location of a pulse.
In order to set the value at the last sample, the option, Last  Pulse  at Last Sample is provided. Otherwise, the last pulse is prior to the last sample.

parameters.label: Number of Pulses
parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The number of pulses to generate.

parameters.label: Interpolate
parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: ⊞  - You can interpolate the values between pulses using the following function curves:

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: nointerp
parameters.description: Disables interpolation.

parameters.label: Linear (Ramp)
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Use linear interpolation between samples when the interval is lengthened. Averages all samples near the new sample when the interval is shortened.

parameters.label: Ease in
parameters.name: easein
parameters.description: Uses an easein() function for blending.

parameters.label: Ease out
parameters.name: easeout
parameters.description: Uses an easeout() function for blending.

parameters.label: Ease in Ease out
parameters.name: cosine
parameters.description: Uses both easein() and easeout() functions.

parameters.label: Cubic
parameters.name: cubic
parameters.description: Cubically interpolates between samples, for smoother curves than Linear. This method is not recommended for channels with sharp changes.

parameters.label: Connect
parameters.name: connect
parameters.description: Instead of the pulses returning to 0, the pulse value is held until the pulse.

parameters.label: Pulse  Width
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: By default, the pulses are a single sample long, but you can increase the  Pulse  Width so that the pulses are steps to the next pulse.

parameters.label: Pulse  Width Unit
parameters.name: widthunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units to use for this parameter, Samples, Frames, or Seconds.

parameters.label: Limit Type
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enable the Minimum and Maximum clamping values below with this menu.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: nolimit
parameters.description: Pulses are allowed to be any value with no clamping.

parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: Clamps pulse values to the Minimum and Maximum values specified below.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: The pulses can be restricted to a Minimum limit. If the Limit Type is Clamp, the graph has additional convenient handles at the minimum for each pulse.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The pulses can be restricted to a Maximum limit. If the Limit Type is Clamp, the graph has additional convenient handles at the maximum for each pulse.

parameters.label: Minimum Spacing
parameters.name: minspacing
parameters.description: When creating pulses via the second input, the Minimum Spacing parameter will separate out pulses from each other with the minimum distance specified here. The unit of the spacing is controlled by the  Pulse  Index Unit parameter.

parameters.label: Cascade when Spacing
parameters.name: cascade
parameters.description: When minimum spacing between pulses is enabled, cascading will shift pulses by the amount of samples added via the minimum spacing.

parameters.label: Outside Pulses
parameters.name: outpulse
parameters.description: Control how to deal with pulse positions specified outside the operators range.

parameters.label: Pulse  Index Unit
parameters.name: pulseunit
parameters.description: Control what unit the in the second input specified values should be interpreted as.

parameters.label: Separate Output Channels
parameters.name: separateoutchan
parameters.description: When toggled on, will create a seperate channel per pulse.

parameters.label: Non-Additives
parameters.name: nonadditives
parameters.description: When enabled will not add up amplitudes of pulses specified on the same sample index.

parameters.label: Last  Pulse  at Last  Sample
parameters.name: lastpulse
parameters.description: In order to set the value at the last sample, the option Last  Pulse  at Last Sample is provided. Otherwise, the last pulse is prior to the last sample.

parameters.label: Pulse
parameters.name: pulse
parameters.description: Sequence of pulse values

parameters.label: Pulse  0
parameters.name: pulse0value
parameters.description: The value of the sequence pulse.

parameters.label: Channel Names
parameters.name: channelname
parameters.description: You can creates many channels with simple patterns like " chan[1-20] ", which generates 20 channels from chan1 to chan20. See the section, Common  CHOP  Parameters for a description of this and all Options. See  Scope and Channel Name Matching  Options.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start of the interval, expressed in Units (seconds, frames or samples).

parameters.label: Start Unit
parameters.name: startunit

parameters.label: End

parameters.label: End Unit
parameters.name: endunit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the units to use for this parameter, Samples, Frames, or Seconds.

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold

parameters.label: Slope

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: cook_time

parameters.label: cook_frame

parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

localNotes.excerpt: *¿Qué hace?** Este operador se encarga de **leer un archivo de geometría** y convertirlo en un formato de POP que se almacena directamente en la **memoria de la GPU** (tarjeta gráfica). * **Características clave:** * Soporta varios formatos de archivo. * Puedes especificar un **URL** (empezando con `http://`) para archivos accesibles en la red. * Tiene una opción para **voltear las caras de la primitiva** (`Flip Primitive Faces`). * Parámetros `Refresh` y `Refresh Pulse` para actualizar los datos del archivo. * Es el punto de partida para cargar geometrías complejas en tu entorno POP. --- #### 26. Force POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador se utiliza principalmente dentro de un **bucle de Particle POP** (operador de partículas) para crear y sumar un conjunto de "fuerzas" que afectan el movimiento de las partículas. La salida es un atributo `float3` llamado `PartForce`. * **Características clave:** * **Fuerzas Globales**: Incluye una fue
